To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
homodimeric NLS peptides with disulfide bond are effective enhancers for liposome-mediated gene transfer.
novel transfection enhancing peptide NLS-CTHd, which is formed by disulfides between two cysteines in SV40 NLS, is more efficient than other peptides in gene transfection with no cytotoxicity.

the novel modified SV40 nuclear localization sequence (NLS) peptides, NLS-CTHC, NLS-NHTD and cyclic NLS peptides, were developed as transfection enhancing peptides to improve the transfection efficiency of cationic-lipid based gene delivery systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
development of new transfection enhancing peptides and their application to gene transfer.
the development of novel non-viral gene carriers based on homodimeric SV 40 NLS peptide.
the development of new gene delivery system with the use of novel SV40 NLS transfection enhancing peptides.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the novel modified SV40 peptides could increase gene transfer efficiency and safety of liposomal delivery systems.
the homodimeric SV 40 NLS peptide (NLS-CHD) is the most effective transfection enhancing peptide for cationic liposome mediated gene transfer among these novel transfecting peptides.
the novel transfection enhancing peptide NLS-CTD is a promising candidate for gene transfer applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the homodimeric NLS peptide with disulfide bond is an efficient non-viral gene transfer enhancer and a novel gene delivery system.
the homodimeric NLS peptides are more efficient than cyclic NLS peptide in gene delivery, and the NLS-CTHd is the most efficient among the three novel peptides.

NLS-CTH homodimeric peptide is the most efficient transfection enhancing peptide among these three novel peptides and it can increase the transfection efficiency of cationic lipid-based non-viral gene transfer vectors without any additional cytotoxicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the novel transfection enhancing peptide, NLS-CTHC, can be easily incorporated into liposomes for the development of a safe and efficient non-viral gene carrier system.
the simple mixing of NLS- CTHD with cationic liposome can enhance transfection potency of cation liposome without cytotoxicity.

the simple modification of NLS peptide by cysteine residue can increase gene transfer potency and the simple mix of NLP with DNA can be an effective strategy for the development of safe and efficient gene delivery system.
